subject: {Disarmed} Density estimation with group size covariate

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: {Disarmed} Density estimation with group size covariate
parts:
Antonela

I can't speak to differences in these results to those in DistWin.  But I find nothing inherently incorrect in the results you have produced.  I've messed around a bit and come up with individual density estimates around 32 animals (I'm guessing per sq km).  Those estimates are robust to truncation distance.  The estimates climb considerably when group size is not a covariate--indicative of size bias, and not the proper analysis to use (as AIC indicates).



library(Distance)
oct12<-read.csv("C:\\Users\\erexs\\Downloads\\oct12R.csv",
                header=TRUE)
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
hist(oct12$distance,main="",xlab="Distance (m)")
hist(oct12$size,main="",xlab="Cluster size")
par(mfrow=c(1,1))
plot(oct12$distance,
     oct12$size, main="", xlab="Distance (m)",ylab="Group size", pch=19, cex=0.5, col=gray(0.7))
oct12$lnsize <- log(oct12$size) # large variation in group size (max>300)
hr800 <- ds(oct12, key="hr", truncation = 800, formula=~size,
            convert.units = 0.001)
hr800ln <- ds(oct12, key="hr", truncation = 800, formula=~lnsize,
              convert.units = 0.001)
hn800ln <- ds(oct12, key="hn", truncation = 800, formula=~lnsize,
              convert.units = 0.001)
hr800.nosize <- ds(oct12, key="hr", truncation = 800, convert.units = 0.001)
summarize_ds_models(hr800, hn800ln, hr800ln, hr800.nosize, output="plain")
hr800.nosize$dht$individuals$D # estimates too high: size bias
hr800ln$dht$individuals$D
hr800$dht$individuals$D
